title: Why Pressure Washing Is the Best Spring Home Investment
seoTitle: Spring Pressure Washing: Refresh Your Home Exterior
seoDescription: How pressure washing removes winter grime, biological growth and road salt residue from exterior surfaces, and what it covers.
html:
After a Canadian winter, the outside of most homes carries road salt spray, mould and mildew growth, organic material and general grime. Pressure washing removes much of it faster than hand scrubbing. It pairs well with a cottage opening inspection or as the first step in a seasonal property maintenance schedule. To have it done, send a request through Collingwood Handyman with photos of the surfaces and your address. A local service provider can review the request and confirm whether the job is within scope.

Beyond Aesthetics: What You Are Removing

The green and black streaks on siding, decks, driveways and walkways are often biological growth, not only dirt. Algae, mould and mildew hold moisture against surfaces. That speeds up rot in wood and wear on painted surfaces. Removing the growth each year helps exterior materials last longer.

Road salt is corrosive and builds up along foundations, driveways and low sections of siding. A thorough spring rinse removes it before it keeps working on concrete, masonry and metal fasteners over the summer.

What Pressure Washing Covers

Most hard exterior surfaces benefit: vinyl, wood and composite siding, concrete and brick driveways and walkways, decks and fences, garage doors, eavestroughs and foundation walls. For surfaces you plan to paint or stain, cleaning first is essential for good adhesion.

Soft washing, which uses lower pressure with a cleaning solution, is the right approach for painted wood, older masonry and roofing materials. High pressure on these surfaces can cause damage. A careful operator adjusts pressure and technique for each surface type.

What to include in your request

List the surfaces, their approximate size, the material, and any loose paint, cracked mortar or damaged siding. Note where outdoor taps are and whether water is available on site. The cost depends on the area, the surface type, the level of growth or staining, access and height. Ask for an itemized written quote, and ask how the provider protects plants, windows and nearby surfaces.
